content:
Following a suggestion by @Kevin Buzzard I am planning on starting a project to formalise CM abelian varieties with a goal to prove the following result:

If A is a CM abelian variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, then it (along with the CM structure) has a model over a number field.

Although I have been playing around with lean for nearly a year, I am new to this, and have some really silly questions. I'll ask my first of many, right now.

Mathlib does show that Abelian varieties are in fact abelian group objects in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Abelian.lean. But, it doesn't have the structure AbelianVarieties defined anywhere (at least as far as I can see). So, I thought I'd start off by defining that, and decided to go with this:

import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Proper
import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Smooth

open AlgebraicGeometry CategoryTheory

variable {K} [Field K] (A : Over (Spec (.of K)))

class AbelianVarieties extends IsProper A.hom, ConnectedSpace A.left, Smooth A.hom, GrpObj A

Is this the right definition to go with? The abelian result I mentioned above, proves the abelianess, when the space is geometrically integral, rather than smooth and connected, the way I defined it. But, 'my' abelian varieties can be shown to be geometrically integral.
I can also define it as reduced instead of smooth, and show that it is smooth. How do I go about choosing the right definition?
My gut feeling is to not worry about that definition for now, but just use the expanded form, similar to Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Abelian.lean.
You could define IsAbelianVariety A but as Johan says, there's no real need for now.

Oh, okay. I shall do that then.
Just out of curiosity, why is this the preferred path though?

One reason is that there are quite a few equivalent definitions, and we haven't really fleshed out the theory around them yet. So locking in on one definition now would prefer one of them over the others, making it harder to formalize certain parts.
I would rather first explore quite a bit more of the theory, show that several definitions are equivalent, and once that is done, survey the resulting sublibrary and decide what is a good definition. By then we can also provide all the API to both produce and consume ab.vars using the equivalent definitions.
In short: we don't have enough theory yet to really claim that we support abelian varieties. Even if there are some small starts.
In particular, working on CM abvars is a great project, but you should realistically expect that you will initially spend the majority of your time working on the general theory of abvars.
Another reason why we tend to prefer the "unbundled spelling" is that it naturally leads to more general statements. For example, the unused argument linter may help you to spot unused assumptions.
